answer: Give every agent a trust score that starts at its nadir: zero. New identities enter through a velvet tier with strict caps on transaction volume and no access to high-value work. To climb, an identity must complete verifiable, useful tasks attested by established peers, and its score decays without continued work. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay the full cost of sustained, attested labor for each fake identity — like forging ferrous parts one by one — while honest agents amortize that cost across a long-lived reputation. Cheap identities stay capped; expensive ones are the point.
